# Complete-consumer bridge for phase-sensitive recoil spectroscopy

Constructed and internally accepted at MODEL/RECEIVER scope: park the optical
logical SPAN in the ground doublet using an ordinary RF swap and allowed
optical shelving; test the actual return, uncat and fluorescence on coherent
recoil histories. A hot arbitrary Hadamard is unnecessary. Smooth BB1 succeeds
in this bounded consumer despite a standalone hot gate error near.03.

Governing assumptions/proof: [MODEL_AND_RECEIVER.md](MODEL_AND_RECEIVER.md).
Primary sources, strongest ordinary comparison, failures and costs:
[PRIOR_AND_COSTS.md](PRIOR_AND_COSTS.md). The source is a pinned public Ca+/CaOH+
model. No added RF, physical Zeeman assignment, new noise parameter, molecular
coherent pulse or measurement was acquired.

The reusable receiver keeps the finite cross-history kernel. Pointwise
unitarity of U(x)=sum_h exp(i h kx)M_h implies PSD coefficient matrix C with
exact diagonal-sum constraints. The complete output is Tr(CK). Quotienting
phase-invisible Toeplitz terms and certifying PSD Gram matrices bounds a
uniform residual D phase without knowing the molecular Hamiltonian or imposing

fixed instrument remain assumptions, not device acquisitions.

# Ground-span parking and a complete finite-history instrument receiver

29 October 2026. Status: constructive source-informed CONTROL MODEL and exact
conditional receiver. A phase-sensitive molecular query has NOT been acquired.
No physical experiment, apparatus modification, shot, or molecular measurement
was performed. The independent A consumer takes the saved kernels as input;
its rational certificate does not validate their ODE or physical acquisition.

## 1. The changed operation and its actual information

The desired resource is complex coherence between two molecular-motion
histories, rather than only a final population or an absorption count. This is
ordinary Ramsey/Loschmidt interferometry when its controlled histories exist.
Here the proposed access is the demonstrated Ca+/CaOH+ recoil-cat apparatus,
with an additional ground-Zeeman RF control and optical shelving/return.

Let a,d denote the optical-qubit basis, |+>,|-> its X eigenstates, and V+,V-
the two motion operators generated by the cat force. With a normalized initial
motion/molecule state rho and spin a, cat--science--uncat gives histories
A+=V+* U V+, A-=V-* U V-. The label coherence is
L=Tr(A-* A+ rho), with a possible conjugation if the label order is reversed.
In the conventional (a,d) Bloch convention, Z=Re L and Y=Im L. X is identically
zero: the cat and its inverse commute with X, and U acts on motion+molecule.
Consequently a tiny X-error is a null-science control, not useful spectroscopy.
`SCIENCE_CHANNEL_CONTROL.json` records this check. Actual finite optical
analyzers are included below, rather than silently identifying them with Pauli
measurements.

Beyond the Lamb--Dicke limit, the V operators in the source model are NOT
assumed to be exact coherent displacements. This does not require arbitrary
independently chosen molecular unitaries U+ and U-. Their access remains the
common physical field sampled by the two cat histories. A generic Hadamard
test identity supplies no such control by itself.

# Optical T2 does not acquire the new parked-memory noise

The source's fitted optical two-level coherence does not identify a unique
generator on the PROPOSED encoding (S-1/2,S+1/2,D-5/2). The cited Wu Methods
III.1--III.3 do not document those numerical Zeeman assignments or the field.
Laser and magnetic noise can agree on the original coherence
while disagreeing on the ground memory. Original0.52 visibility is not assigned
to this sequence.

An explicit SCENARIO uses independent magnetic and optical-phase Markov noise:
sqrt(f/(2T))*diag(-1,+1,-3) and sqrt((1-f)/(2T))*diag(+1,+1,-1), f in[0,1].
Their optical S-/D decay is1/T, ground S-/S+ decayf/T, and S+/D decay(1+3f)/T.
Equal magnetic sensitivity is useful only within this specified noise model.
An independent sqrt(2*gamma)*|S+><S+| dephaser leaves original optical qubit
calibration unchanged while adding gamma to S+ coherence decay. Optical T2
alone therefore bounds neither gamma nor the full new instrument. This is
an identification boundary, not an assertion that the apparatus has that fault.

Important source qualification: Wu et al., arXiv:2511.19687v2, III.3 explicitly
attribute their physical model to magnetic-field and trap-voltage fluctuations,
with Ramsey Tspin=2.8(3)ms and Tmotion=85(+98/-35)ms. They also fit an extra-wait
visibility decay tau_d=0.92(6)ms. Thus f=1,gamma=0 is a conditional extension of
their stated magnetic-noise model to the proposed three-level encoding; it is
not an arbitrary favorable embedding. Neither their stated assumption nor the
two-level Ramsey fit measures the parked ground-doublet coherence or establishes
noise completeness for added RF/optical controls. No source contrast or tau_d is
assigned to the new sequence. Primary: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.19687v2 .

noisy_kernel_model.py is an UNEXECUTED scenario library. Its current constructor
NativeModel(magnetic_fraction,extra_ground_rate,N=100,rtol=1e-7) requires f,gamma
explicitly; it has no default for either. No fixed favorable-noise run, noisy kernel or measured parkedT2
is claimed. It is not a governing positive result. The kernel receiver accepts
a separately warranted full-instrument error budget, including noise, all
modes, other Zeeman edges and analysis/readout. That budget is not supplied by
the source. A loaded apparatus experiment is outside authorized actions.
